reported_failure: iOS/Safari WebContent process crash when selecting an expanded PDF page thumbnail; subsequent PDF entry can repeatedly crash; PDF collection may disappear from Today’s Reading.

diagnosis.screenshot_classification: Safari/WebKit process-level page failure (the browser reports that a problem repeatedly occurred), not an ordinary caught in-app error.
code_root_causes: Build 108 replaced the PDF DOM before clearing the previous PDF runtime on PDF-to-PDF navigation, allowing detached canvases/render work and the new PDF view to overlap.
The full-page IntersectionObserver was attached before resume navigation and used a 1200px root margin; a later fallback also forced pages 1 and 2 to render, increasing transient canvas pressure.
Offscreen pages that became non-visible while still loading could finish with a full canvas and remain allocated.
The ink overlay allocated a second full-resolution canvas even when no ink existed.
The thumbnail sheet opened another PDF.js document while the main PDF renderer remained active, and thumbnail document destruction was deliberately delayed, increasing transition overlap.
Build 108 browser navigation tests stubbed PDF.js canvas rendering and therefore could not exercise iOS WebKit process-memory behavior.
PDF-only original-view activity was not incorporated into readingProgressInfo/last-opened state, so a no-plan PDF collection could disappear from Today’s Reading after process restart.
